items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex desktop on Windows, using the official Plugin Creator integration to update an owned private personal (`USER`-scoped) account plugin. The installed `plugin-creator:update-plugin` skill package is version `0.1.22`; this is the plugin package version, not the desktop app version.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please support explicit removal of retired files and directories when updating an account plugin, while preserving its identity, ownership, sharing, connected app bindings, and unrelated assets.

Plugin Creator's current `update_plugin` tool documents overlay-only behavior:

> For both personal and workspace plugins, uploaded files overlay the current release; omitted files and binary assets remain intact.

> This tool cannot delete files.

The corresponding installed update instructions also explicitly say that a complete archive cannot delete files. The exposed update arguments are `archive`, `expected_release_id`, and `plugin_id`; there is no deletion list or replacement mode.

This makes a normal skill rename incomplete: the new skill can be published, but the old `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, metadata, and supporting files cannot be retired from the published package through this editor.

### Additional information

#### Reproduction scenario

1. Create an owned private personal plugin with `skills/old-name/SKILL.md` and `skills/old-name/agents/openai.yaml`.
2. Rename the skill locally to `skills/new-name/`, update its metadata, and bump the plugin version.
3. Prepare a complete ZIP containing the intended new package, without `skills/old-name/`.
4. Update the existing plugin using its current release ID as `expected_release_id`.
5. Inspect the published release using `get_plugin_files`, then refresh the installed plugin.

Under the documented overlay behavior, the retired paths remain in the release. Omitting them from the ZIP cannot express deletion.

#### Observed in our workflow

We recently standardized a plugin's skill names and source layout. On October 1, 2026, a read-back of the resulting private account release still contained the two retired skill directories alongside the three canonical skills.

Because deletion is explicitly unsupported, we overwrote the old skills with short migration notices and set `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` in their metadata. The read-back confirmed those notices and policies. This is containment: the retired paths still exist in the published release. We did not perform a separate omission-only upload as part of this report, since the tool explicitly documents that it cannot remove files.

#### Requested behavior

Either of these would address the problem:

- An explicit `delete_paths` operation on the guarded update, with plugin-relative paths and recursive directory removal.
- An opt-in complete-package replacement mode, where omission removes old files and the caller supplies every component intended to remain.

Please retain overlay updates as the default. Apply deletion atomically with the new release and the existing release-ID guard, validate that deletion stays within the package, and expose the resulting file inventory for verification.

If there is already a supported route for a private personal plugin to remove paths while preserving the existing identity and app bindings, please document it in Plugin Creator's tool contract and update instructions.

#### Scope and routing

This concerns the account publishing service/editor used from Codex, rather than a local plugin cache bug. Restarting Codex or creating a fresh chat cannot remove files that still exist in the published release. Related client cache work such as https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/42284 addresses a different layer.

The developer portal documents complete ZIP package updates at https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission, and GitHub migration is documented for workspace plugins at https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/plugin-management. Neither establishes an available deletion route for this private personal plugin through Plugin Creator.

If another OpenAI team owns this publisher capability, please route the request there or identify the appropriate tracker.

items.title: [ChatGPT Web] Intermittent message stream errors with web research + GitHub plugin since Oct 1

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

ChatGPT **Chat on the web** intermittently terminates with **“메시지 스트림에 오류 발생” (“Error in message stream”)** when a single request combines web research with investigation through the connected GitHub plugin. The issue was first noticed on **October 1, 2026, KST (UTC+9)** and recurred during ordinary use in Chrome and Safari.

A fresh, dedicated reproduction using an OpenAI careers question failed before the final answer. Two differently worded prompts completed in the same Chrome session. This is intermittent, not a claim that every combined-tool request fails.

**Surface:** chatgpt.com → Chat, not Work or the Codex CLI. Filing here because this tracker already contains ChatGPT web/integration reports; please route to the appropriate Chat owner if needed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a ChatGPT account with GitHub already connected.
2. Open a new **Chat** on chatgpt.com.
3. Select the GitHub plugin in the composer. For the measured runs, the model was GPT-5.6 Sol and the reasoning level was High.
4. Submit a prompt below that requires current web research and GitHub project inspection in the same turn.
5. Observe the tool activity and whether a final answer completes. The failure is intermittent.

**Prompt A — failed in the measured run**

> OpenAI의 현재 채용공고를 웹에서 확인하고, 연결된 GitHub의 내 프로젝트를 조사해서 매칭되는 공고가 있는지 알려줘.

English equivalent: Check OpenAI's current job postings on the web, investigate my projects through the connected GitHub account, and tell me whether any roles match.

**Prompt B — completed in the measured run**

> OpenAI가 지금 어떤 개발자를 채용하는지 웹에서 조사해줘. GitHub에서 내 프로젝트를 확인하고 채용 요건과 비교해줘.

English equivalent: Research on the web which developers OpenAI is hiring now. Check my projects on GitHub and compare them with the job requirements.

**Prompt C — completed in the measured run**

> 내 GitHub 프로젝트와 관련 있는 OpenAI 채용공고가 있나? 최신 공고를 웹에서 찾고 저장소의 구현 내용을 근거로 판단해줘.

English equivalent: Are any OpenAI job postings relevant to my GitHub projects? Find current postings on the web and assess them using the repository implementations.

### What is the expected behavior?

Complete the combined investigation and deliver the final answer. If a tool call fails, expose a specific recoverable error instead of losing the response to a generic message-stream error.

### Additional information

#### Directly measured fresh-chat tests

All three were run **sequentially**, once per prompt, in separate new chats on the same Chrome/Plus setup. GPT-5.6 Sol was checked in the model picker before the first run; High was visible before every submission. No model change was made between runs. Browser version has not been recorded.

| Prompt | Start, October 1, 2026 (KST) | Result | Time from Send invocation to error/completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 19:36:40.955 | Message stream error; no final answer | 55.3–56.4 seconds |
| B | 19:38:27.561 | Final answer completed | 330.0–331.1 seconds |
| C | 19:44:07.559 | Final answer completed | 340.4–341.8 seconds |

For A, the assistant first announced research of official OpenAI roles and GitHub projects. The last activity line was:

> GitHub 프로필과 저장소 및 OpenAI 채용공고를 조사함

English: Researched the GitHub profile/repositories and OpenAI job postings.

It then displayed the stream error before a final answer. A screenshot of this new reproduction is retained locally. The status text alone does not prove that every underlying tool call succeeded.

**Timing method:** the start timestamp was recorded immediately before invoking the Send button through browser automation. The rendered DOM was observed approximately once per second within observation batches. Each interval brackets the last non-terminal observation and the first observation showing the error or a completed answer. These are client-side UI timings, not server execution or network timings. No HAR, request ID, or failing HTTP status was captured.

#### Other observed comparisons (not timed in the three runs above)

- The original combined web-research/GitHub question failed in Chrome and Safari. Safari failure is documented in a screenshot supplied by the reporter.
- The reporter tested the same original question in the ChatGPT desktop app → Chat and obtained completed answers on both Plus and Pro accounts. The desktop app version was not recorded.
- A directly observed iPhone 16 test in the ChatGPT mobile app → Chat completed a final answer with web research and the GitHub plugin in the same turn. Details below.
- A web-only company-research request completed in Chrome.
- In an earlier failed web chat, navigating away and returning removed the visible error banner while leaving only the incomplete response and tool activity. The original screenshot preserved the error.

These comparisons were not a fully controlled cross-client experiment: exact app/browser versions, historical model settings, and network conditions were not all captured. They suggest a web-path investigation is useful, but do not prove a browser-specific or server-side cause. GitHub-only behavior has not been systematically tested.

#### Mobile app check — completed answer, not a precise speed comparison

On October 1, 2026, an iPhone 16 running the ChatGPT mobile app → Chat was observed through macOS iPhone Mirroring. The GitHub plugin was visibly selected. The reporter stated that the existing settings were already matched; the mobile account tier, exact model, reasoning level, app version, and iOS version were not independently recorded.

A fresh chat submitted this English equivalent of Prompt A:

> Check OpenAI's current job postings on the web, investigate my projects through the connected GitHub account, and tell me whether any roles match.

The confirmed Send action (Return key) started at **20:08:29.714 KST**. Web-search activity and GitHub project investigation were visibly observed, followed by a complete final answer with response actions and the composer returned to its idle voice control. No message-stream error was visible in the completed result.

The last observed generating state was in an observation starting approximately **256.4 seconds** after Send; a completed state was observed by **307.7 seconds**. Mirroring disconnected during the run and individual screenshot calls also introduced observation delays, so this broad interval is **not a precise completion-time measurement or a valid web-versus-mobile speed comparison**. It is evidence that this single mobile combined-tool request completed. English wording also differs from the Korean web test. Further mobile timing/repeat tests were stopped at the reporter's request after successful completion was confirmed.

#### Possible regression window — hypothesis, not established cause

Around October 1 (KST), the reporter also noticed Chat becoming substantially faster/more responsive. That perceived change coincided with the onset of these failures. There is no before/after latency baseline, so this is a useful chronology signal rather than a measured performance claim.

The [official ChatGPT release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes) list September 29 changes including GPT-6.1 Sol in **Work and Codex** and plugin extensions. They do not establish a corresponding GPT-5.6 Sol Chat speed update on October 1 or a causal link to this failure. The September 14 retirement of automatic Instant-to-Thinking switching also does not establish the cause of a run explicitly showing High.

The [official DevDay 2026 recap](https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap/), dated September 29, announces GPT-6.1 Sol, Ultrafast, and plugin ecosystem changes. The announced Ultrafast availability concerns API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work tiers; it does not establish an October 1 speed upgrade to ordinary Chat using GPT-5.6 Sol. The release window is worth correlating with the onset, but no causal connection has been established.

Please check whether web Chat deployments, experiment/feature-flag assignments, model routing, or tool-result/stream handling changes around this window correlate with the failures. The one ~56-second failure is insufficient evidence for a fixed timeout.

#### Scope of the evidence

This is a useful intermittent reproduction report, not a root-cause determination or failure-rate estimate. Each wording was run only once, and model/tool behavior can vary. The observed 1 failure in 3 runs should not be treated as a population failure rate or proof that wording caused the difference. A same-prompt repeat test and matched web-only/GitHub-only/combined controls would be needed to isolate the trigger further.

Existing issues were searched for the message-stream error, GitHub plus web research, and Safari. Related general stream-error reports were found, but no exact duplicate matching this combination and comparison was identified.

This report intentionally excludes previous personal conversations, account email, private repository contents, and shared conversation links.

items.body:
### Environment

Windows x64, official Microsoft Store Codex Desktop package `26.928.3736.0`. This is a Desktop authentication-state report, rather than a CLI prompt/model issue.

### Observed behavior and limits of the evidence

During intermittent network failures, the entire Desktop application returned to the sign-in screen. Logs in the surrounding failure windows include TLS handshake EOF, request timeouts and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`. The inspected logs did not contain an explicit `invalid_grant`, revoked/reused/invalidated refresh-token error.

I have **not** established the exact branch that caused that particular UI transition: the relevant Desktop auth-transition events were not captured. Token validity before the incident is also unconfirmed. The component-level reproductions below are deterministic, but are not an end-to-end reproduction of the login-screen transition.

### Deterministic component reproductions in the installed bundle

I extracted the following functions from the original installed `resources/app.asar`, evaluated them with Node's `vm`, and injected transport failures using synthetic fixtures only. No real credentials or network calls were used.

1. **Forced token retrieval clears cached identity on a transient exception.**

   In `.vite/build/bootstrap-DvSEn4qy.js`, `fetchAuthToken(refreshToken, generation)` catches any exception and, if the generation still matches, calls `setAuthTokenCache(null)` before rethrowing. There is no distinction between a transport failure and a permanent authentication rejection in this catch.

   With a synthetic cached token whose expiry is ten minutes in the future, and `requestAuthStatus` throwing an Error with `code = "ECONNRESET"`, calling `fetchAuthToken(true)` clears the cache. The actual setter publishes an authenticated-principal change from present to null.

   Control: `refreshCachedAuthTokenAsync` with the same cached-token fixture and transport error preserves the cache and publishes no principal change. This difference between background and forced refresh seems relevant.

2. **A failed refresh on a 401-retry path is wrapped as another 401, even when its own failure is a connection reset.**

   In `.vite/build/main-DkWgQSQe.js`, `xue` catches `getAuthToken` errors and wraps them as `new A_(failureMessage, errorStatus, cause)`. When called by the authenticated request's 401-retry path with `errorStatus: 401` and `refreshToken: true`, a refresh transport error produces `status: 401, cause.code: "ECONNRESET"`.

   This is conditional on entering the original 401 retry; it is **not** a claim that every network failure becomes a 401 or that the original server response was spurious.

3. **Account-summary retrieval converts a temporary failure into a successful "no token" result.**

   In the same main bundle, `k_` catches a failure from `getConnection(...).getAuthToken({refreshToken:false})`, logs "Unable to extract account id and plan from auth token", and returns a summary with `hasChatGptToken:false` and null account fields instead of propagating the error.

   A temporary app-server/transport failure is therefore represented like an unauthenticated account. This reproduction injects failure directly at token retrieval; it does not assume that normal retrieval of an already-valid cache necessarily makes a network request.

### Fixture results

```json
{
  "sourceVersion": "26.928.3736.0",
  "forcedRefresh": {
    "networkError": "ECONNRESET",
    "cachePreserved": false,
    "principalChanges": [
      {"previousPresent": true, "currentPresent": false}
    ]
  },
  "backgroundRefresh": {
    "cachePreserved": true,
    "principalChanges": []
  },
  "httpRetryWrapper": {
    "status": 401,
    "causeCode": "ECONNRESET"
  },
  "accountSummaryOnNetworkFailure": {
    "hasChatGptToken": false,
    "accountMissing": true,
    "errorPropagated": false
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

Temporary transport/app-server unavailability should remain distinguishable from confirmed credential invalidation and explicit sign-out. Preserve a still-valid cached identity where appropriate; never return an expired access token as usable. A failed refresh caused by transport trouble should not itself be reported as a confirmed authentication rejection, and account-summary callers should receive a retryable error/state rather than a successful "no token" result.

Permanent invalidation, account changes, explicit logout and a successful response explicitly reporting no token must still follow the intended authentication transitions.

### Additional validation

An isolated, version-specific local copy with narrow changes to these three paths passed offline checks for:
- preserving cache on transient failures;
- refusing to return expired cached tokens;
- retaining permanent-error and explicit-missing-token behavior;
- distinguishing a transport refresh failure from 401;
- propagating temporary account-summary retrieval errors.

That copy has **not** been activated or tested against the live Desktop UI. The observed incident occurred using the official installation. These offline checks are supporting evidence for the state-handling issue, not a production fix claim.

Related reports: #40761 and #40815 (both currently open). Their symptoms overlap, but this report adds component-level transport-failure reproductions for this newer Windows Desktop package.

No tokens, account identifiers, personal IP addresses or private raw logs are included.

### Observed behavior

A valid local V2 custom pet is installed but absent from the pet list in Codex Desktop on Windows with WSL agent execution.

Investigated Windows package: 26.928.3736.0.

### Diagnostic results

The same pet package was tested with the installed loader, bundled manifest schema, and path converter:

| Harness case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Windows process, Windows paths | Pet discovered |
| Linux process, POSIX paths | Pet discovered |
| Windows process, POSIX path operations, Windows-style pet root | Pet omitted |

In the failing case, directory enumeration succeeds. POSIX path resolution treats the Windows-style root as a relative path and embeds it under the process working directory. The installed converter then produces a nonexistent WSL UNC path. Reading the manifest returns `ENOENT`; the loader catches the error and omits the pet.

These results reproduce a loader path-handling defect. They come from the diagnostic harness, not a trace of the running application's IPC.

### Expected behavior

A valid local pet should be discovered. The loader should use a root and path operations with matching path syntax, and report manifest-read failures rather than silently omitting the pet.

### Recurrence

The same missing-pet symptom in WSL mode was reported in #20905, which was closed as completed. In my experience, the problem returns periodically and remains unresolved for weeks. Please investigate the recurrence and add regression coverage for the Windows-process/WSL-host path boundary.

# Windows desktop startup remains on loading animation; Mobile Remote renderer reset restores UI

## Version and platform
Collected 2026-10-01. Windows 11 Pro 25H2 x64, 10.0.26200.9457. Microsoft Store/MSIX package OpenAI.Codex 26.928.3736.0. Installed desktop app.asar package.json release 26.928.31416 (read-only inspection). Bundled/running CLI 0.159.2. Latest desktop performance logs: build 12553, commit 69c39c76da78edf143e380efffe94e49f10da8e0. Prior affected package 26.924.2738.0, desktop release 26.924.22138/build 11645. Package, desktop release and internal build are separate version fields. Subscription: ChatGPT Pro.

## Impact and reproduction
The user reports that every app restart now remains on the startup loading animation on two Windows machines, both with Remote enabled. The desktop cannot be used until renderer processes are reset from a task accessed through Mobile Remote. Only one machine's logs and environment were collected for this package; the second machine is user-reported and its precise environment is unavailable.

1. Enable Remote on the Windows desktop app and use it normally.
2. Exit and relaunch the desktop app.
3. Observe persistent startup loading animation instead of the usable shell/sidebar.
4. Access the desktop task through Mobile Remote; the backend remains accessible.
5. Terminate the verified ChatGPT.exe renderer child processes only, preserving the main ChatGPT.exe and codex.exe app-server.
6. The app automatically creates replacement renderers and finishes loading.

Expected: normal startup without manual process intervention. If initialization cannot complete, show an actionable error and recover.

The frequency of every restart is the user's current report. Historical logs also contain successful starts; this is not a claim that every retained startup span failed. Remote being enabled on both machines is a common factor, not a proven cause. No Remote-disabled A/B test has been performed.

## Diagnostic evidence (UTC)
| Main process/session | Startup timeout | Successful startup after reset | Duration after reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| PID 16544, Sep 27 | 2026-09-27 20:05:26.882 | 2026-09-27 20:40:22.159 | 5131.2 ms |
| PID 11440, Sep 29 | 2026-09-29 03:03:27.762 | 2026-09-29 08:32:56.960 | 5658.1 ms |
| PID 14276, Sep 30 | 2026-09-30 12:57:49.357 | 2026-09-30 13:53:17.431 | 6465.1 ms |
| PID 13188, Oct 1 | 2026-10-01 03:03:30.489 | 2026-10-01 08:05:37.583 | 6022.3 ms |
| PID 416, Oct 1 | 2026-10-01 08:08:11.756 | 2026-10-01 08:09:01.108 | 6331.0 ms |

Latest failure, build 12553: `name=app_start outcome=failure reason=timeout durationMs=122867.1`. Marks: renderer_entry_evaluated 2847.7, host_services_ready 2897, renderer_ready 3172.7, host_startup_ready 3176.7, settings_ready 3577.7 ms. shell_visible, home_visible and sidebar_ready are absent. Primary window visible; webContentsId=1/windowId=1.

Same session after renderer reset: `name=app_start outcome=success durationMs=6331`, shell_visible 5914.2, home_visible 5914.3, sidebar_ready 6331 ms. Verified recovery reset at 08:08:53.828Z: renderers 17156/6260/13708 replaced by 17348/17340; original main PID 416 and app-server PID 6200 remained running with unchanged creation identities. A secondary non-app-server codex process exited automatically during recovery; preservation is claimed for the original app-server, not every transient process.

Earlier Sep 29 failure: timeout 123328.8 ms despite renderer_ready 3631.7, host_startup_ready 3635.9 and settings_ready 4034.9 ms. After resetting the main renderer only, shell/home became visible at about 5180 ms and sidebar at 5658 ms in the same main process session.

The retained desktop logs contain 29 app_start spans, including nine failures. Full per-span timeline and source file/line numbers are included. The log's timeout is a telemetry deadline; the UI remains stuck beyond that deadline until intervention.

## Recovery mechanism and previous interventions
Main process: installed Store ChatGPT.exe without a --type argument. UI children: same executable with --type=renderer. Recovery uses a fixed, revalidated process snapshot, stopping renderer PIDs only; no process tree termination. Renderer-client-id must be inspected each time, not hardcoded. Later recovery resets all current app renderers, which can also refresh browser/detached views.

On package 26.924.2738.0, read-only inspection of installed app.asar found maybeRecoverFromRendererCrash in .vite/build/main-DAwJoFgo.js: for non-clean renderer loss, while the app is not quitting and the window is alive, schedule webContents.reload after 500 ms; did-finish-load clears the recovery-attempt guard. Observed replacement and successful startup corroborate recovery. No installed app code was modified.

Ctrl+R did not recover the issue on the other machine (user report). Whole-app restart does not provide lasting recovery. No cache/settings deletion, conversation deletion, reinstall, or new renderer reset was performed during this collection.

A prior community workaround, GoMaaars/codex-desktop-send-button-fix, was used for a related local-config/send-button blockage on Sep 24. It reissued pending startup requests and recovered workspace availability without a renderer reload. Its log showed pending locale-info, get-global-state, inbox-items, list-automations, codex-command-keymap-state, codex-home, paths-exist, and global-dictation-hotkey-state requests. This is earlier diagnostic context, not proof the current startup hang has the same initiating cause. Existing watcher logs from Sep 23 were also found and preserved; no workaround was installed or activated for this collection. A later inspector-based attempt failed. No binary patch was applied.

## Requested investigation
Please investigate primary renderer startup initialization/state delivery, including startup with Remote enabled, slow backend initialization, and first launch after updates. The backend remains accessible while the visible UI loading gate does not finish. Renderer recreation resolves it in the same main/backend process session. Ensure initialization eventually reaches the renderer or is retried safely rather than leaving the UI on an indefinite animation. These observations localize the symptom but do not prove a root cause.

Related reports: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48484, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49557, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48558, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48216. This report adds repeated recovery pairs on build 12553 and two-machine recurrence with Remote enabled. No initialization-handshake replay was performed on this machine during this collection; #49557's replay evidence belongs to that reporter.

## Package scope and privacy
All discovered retained desktop logs (Sep 17–Oct 1) and existing workaround logs were copied into a separate PRIVATE-local-only directory with file sizes and SHA-256 hashes. Raw process command lines and codex doctor JSON are private. No CLI log directory was present at the checked ~/.codex/log path; no runtime logs were found under the checked Local OpenAI/Codex runtime tree. No second-machine logs are available. Live log copies are a point-in-time snapshot and may grow afterward.

The shareable ZIP contains this report, environment metadata, startup timeline, selected startup/handshake/renderer lifecycle excerpts with source line numbers, and a reduced doctor summary. It excludes auth files, cookies, settings databases, conversation transcripts, crash dumps, raw process command lines and raw logs. Private identifiers/paths/URLs are omitted from excerpts. Full originals remain local for further targeted review if Support requests additional evidence.

CLI doctor was run after recovery, so its results cannot establish health during the hang. It reports configured auth and a successful desktop app-server handshake. Its separate daemon-not-running check refers to the standalone background daemon, not the live desktop stdio app-server. Optional configuration warnings should not be assumed to explain the renderer hang.

Codex can list and bind tabs from the identified browser instances, or returns an actionable diagnostic identifying the failing bridge component.

Please help identify why browser discovery succeeds but subsequent browser-control requests time out. Is there a supported diagnostic for this transport failure, a known affected build, or a confirmed fix?

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
**What variant of Codex are you using?**

Codex App (macOS desktop, bundled CLI 0.159.0), also applies to any long-running `codex app-server` / TUI session

**What feature would you like to see?**

A supported way to make a running app-server (and the Desktop model picker) re-read `model_catalog_json` without restarting the process.

**Motivation.** `model_catalog_json` is a documented integration point for proxies and custom providers (we run a local routing proxy that rewrites the catalog file when its provider table changes). Today the catalog is captured in memory at process start and nothing can refresh it:

- `StaticModelsManager` is built once from `config.model_catalog` at startup (`codex-rs/app-server/src/message_processor.rs` via `build_models_manager`, `codex-rs/core/src/thread_manager.rs`) and `StaticModelsManager::raw_model_catalog` ignores every `RefreshStrategy` (`codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs`).
- `reload_user_config` (the hot-reload path behind `config/batchWrite` with `reloadUserConfig: true`) rebuilds `Config` objects for loaded threads, but `ThreadManager.state.models_manager` is never replaced, so the picker keeps serving the startup catalog.
- The background `ModelsRefreshWorker` (every 4.5 min) calls `list_models(RefreshStrategy::Online)`, which is a no-op for the static manager.
- There are no POSIX-signal handlers for config/catalog reload (only SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown in `codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/stdio.rs`).

**Live experiment confirming the gap.** We started an app-server pointed at a 26-model catalog, then updated the same file to 30 models (4 new) and called `config/batchWrite` with `edits: []` and `reloadUserConfig: true`. The RPC returned `status: ok` (config reload succeeded, config.toml untouched), but `model/list` still returned 26 models and none of the new ones. New threads did not see the new models either, because session model resolution goes through the same captured manager (`codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs`).

**What we currently have to do:** fully restart the Desktop app (or the daemon) after every catalog change. Short-lived processes (`codex exec`, fresh TUI connections) pick up the new file immediately, which makes the staleness confusing to diagnose — behavior differs per surface.

**Proposals (any one would unblock us):**

1. An app-server RPC such as `model/catalog/reload` that rebuilds the models manager from the current `model_catalog_json` and pushes a picker-update notification to connected clients.
2. A file watcher / mtime check on the catalog path consulted by `model/list` (perhaps gated behind a config flag).
3. Making `StaticModelsManager` honor a `RefreshStrategy::Online` by re-reading the file, so the existing `ModelsRefreshWorker` picks changes up within its 4.5-minute interval.

**Additional information**

Related existing issues that describe symptoms of the same root cause, from different angles:

- #43052 — stale `model_catalog_json` silently hides newly launched models (Desktop launch blocker)
- #47917 — catalog resolved once at startup; `context_window` cannot follow a provider switch
- #34487 — custom models from `model_catalog_json` not shown in Desktop picker
- #48697 — stale catalog keeps the Desktop picker on an older model family

All of these would be mitigated by a reload capability; today the only remediation is a process restart, which is hard to automate for a desktop app and easy to forget.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop on macOS fails to initialize my authenticated workspace when launched normally from Finder/Dock.

The main error is:

```text
Sign-in failed: workspace routing discovery timed out
```

The application logs show `account/read` consistently taking about 15 seconds and then failing:

```text
[AppServerConnection] response_routed
durationMs=15002
errorCode=-32603
method=account/read

[electron-message-handler] Request failed
durationMs=15060
error={"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery timed out"}
method=account/read
```

I have also observed:

```text
Workspace routing is unavailable
```

with HTTP status `432` on requests including:

```text
/settings/user
/wham/usage
/wham/tasks/list
```

On some login attempts, the logs also contain:

```text
Authenticated workspace changed
account_login_completed ... success=false
```

My ChatGPT authentication itself is still valid.

The important A/B test is:

### Normal launch

Launching Codex normally from Finder/Dock fails with workspace routing discovery timeout.

### Electron proxy flag only

Launching with:

```bash
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT \
  --proxy-server=http://127.0.0.1:7897
```

does NOT fix the problem.

`account/read` still takes approximately 15 seconds and fails with:

```text
workspace routing discovery timed out
```

### HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY

Launching the same app with:

```bash
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 \
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT
```

works.

Codex opens normally and immediately recognizes the already signed-in ChatGPT account.

This machine previously worked normally without manually setting these environment variables.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run a local HTTP proxy on:

```text
127.0.0.1:7897
```

2. Confirm that ChatGPT/network access through the proxy is working.

For example:

```bash
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
  -o /dev/null \
  -sS \
  -w 'DNS:%{time_namelookup}\nCONNECT:%{time_connect}\nTLS:%{time_appconnect}\nTTFB:%{time_starttransfer}\nTOTAL:%{time_total}\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n' \
  https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/accounts/check
```

Example result on my machine:

```text
DNS:0.000073
CONNECT:0.000654
TLS:0.214420
TTFB:0.470486
TOTAL:0.470563
HTTP:401
```

The `401` is expected because this curl request does not contain my ChatGPT authentication token. The relevant point is that the endpoint is reachable in less than one second.

3. Launch Codex normally from Finder/Dock.

4. Codex fails during account/workspace initialization with:

```text
workspace routing discovery timed out
```

5. Quit Codex completely.

6. Launch with only the Electron proxy option:

```bash
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT \
  --proxy-server=http://127.0.0.1:7897
```

7. The same timeout still occurs.

8. Quit Codex again.

9. Launch with explicit proxy environment variables:

```bash
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 \
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT
```

10. Codex initializes successfully and the existing authenticated account is recognized.

No model request/session is reached before the failure, so token limit/context-window usage is not applicable.

### What is the expected behavior?

## What is the expected behavior?

Codex Desktop should restore and initialize the existing authenticated ChatGPT workspace when launched normally from Finder/Dock.

Users should not need to inject `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` manually into the GUI application's environment.

If the Desktop application is using a proxy, the bundled Codex CLI/app-server should use a compatible proxy configuration as well.

In particular, proxy handling should be consistent between the Electron/Desktop networking layer and the bundled Codex app-server.

### Additional information

This appears to be related specifically to proxy propagation/discovery between Codex Desktop and its bundled Codex CLI/app-server.

The bundled runtime is launched by Desktop from:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex
```

The app-server initializes successfully, but `account/read` later waits approximately 15 seconds before workspace routing fails.

A particularly useful observation is:

```text
--proxy-server=http://127.0.0.1:7897
```

alone does not fix the problem, while:

```text
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897
```

does.

This suggests that the failing workspace-routing request is likely made by the bundled Codex CLI/app-server process and is not using the same proxy configuration as the Electron network stack.

This setup previously worked normally on the same Mac without manually injecting HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY.

### Summary

On Windows, the ChatGPT desktop app could not be opened normally, and rebooting did not resolve the problem. Launching the installed app with a process-local CODEX_CLI_PATH pointing to its own bundled Codex 0.159.2 restored startup. The app's server process started, the window became responsive, and the user confirmed that the app opened successfully.

This is an observed recovery, not a confirmed root-cause diagnosis.

### Environment

- Date observed: 2026-10-01 (Asia/Seoul)
- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300, x64
- Installed Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.928.3736.0
- Bundled Codex CLI: 0.159.2, verified by running the package's app/resources/codex.exe --version
- Separately installed Codex resolved by the terminal: 0.153.4
- A legacy manually copied runtime existed at version 0.155.0-alpha.9.2.
- At the start of this investigation, the user-level CODEX_CLI_PATH and CODEX_HOME overrides were unset. There is no evidence that the legacy copy was selected during the failing default startup.

### Observed behavior

1. Normal startup failed to produce a usable app; the user reported that the issue persisted after reboot.
2. Get-AppxPackage reported the installed package as OK.
3. The bundled codex.exe existed and its --version command succeeded.
4. Diagnostic launches without explicitly selecting the bundled CLI did not restore a usable app.
5. A launch explicitly selecting the package's own codex.exe started an app-server from that same package. The app window subsequently became responsive, and the user confirmed successful startup.

### Successful recovery

The following variables were changed only in the launcher process. No user-level or machine-level environment variables were changed:

```powershell
$package = Get-AppxPackage -Name OpenAI.Codex |
    Sort-Object Version -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 1

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE', $null, 'Process')
$env:CODEX_CLI_PATH = Join-Path $package.InstallLocation 'app\resources\codex.exe'
Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $package.InstallLocation 'app\ChatGPT.exe')
```

ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 was present in the diagnostic shell inherited from VS Code; it was cleared for launches before the successful attempt. Clearing it alone had not restored the app. This does not establish that it affected startup from the Start menu.

No runtime binaries were copied or replaced in this recovery. A local recovery launcher resolves the currently installed package on each invocation, rather than pinning an old copied binary.

### Limits and requested investigation

- We have not confirmed which CLI or other runtime component the default startup selected.
- We have not reproduced the issue on a clean machine.
- A reboot or fresh default startup after recovery has not yet been tested.
- A later attempt using an ASCII home path reused the already-running recovered app, so it does not establish that changing CODEX_HOME was necessary.
- Please investigate the normal Windows startup/runtime resolution and registration path when multiple Codex versions exist, and why explicitly selecting the bundled runtime restores startup.

Related startup reports: #28392 and #40776. This report does not establish the same WSL-specific cause as #40776.

No account information, raw logs, session transcripts, or personal filesystem paths are included.

items.body:
# Idle IDE chat repeatedly remounts and interrupts IME composition when account-query errors change

## What version of the IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt`, stable version `26.928.31416`.

The behavior also occurred before switching from a preview installation to stable. Switching to stable did not by itself resolve it.

## What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT sign-in. The subscription tier has not been recorded for this report.

## Which IDE are you using?

VS Code `1.135.0` on macOS, using Remote SSH to a Linux server.

## What platform is your computer?

Local: `Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm` (`uname -mprs`). Remote extension host: Linux x86_64.

## What issue are you seeing?

An authenticated local chat visibly flickered approximately every 3–4 seconds, including while idle. Its transcript briefly disappeared and returned. The composer DOM node was repeatedly replaced, interrupting Chinese IME composition: after a few characters, the composition could become unconverted pinyin.

The extension host also logged repeated account-query fetch failures. I do not claim that all network failures cause this issue, or that every error/retry transition was individually timestamp-correlated.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed reproduction conditions (not yet a minimal deterministic reproduction):

1. Use VS Code on macOS with a Linux Remote SSH extension host and the extension version above.
2. Sign in with ChatGPT and open an existing local conversation in the Codex IDE webview.
3. In the affected environment, account-query requests repeatedly fail/retry. Leave the conversation idle and observe its transcript and composer for at least 20 seconds.
4. Try composing a sentence with a Chinese IME. During the flicker, the composer can be recreated and composition is interrupted.

## What is the expected behavior?

Account-metadata fetch errors and retries should not unmount the active conversation or replace its composer DOM node. The transcript should remain visible and IME composition should continue uninterrupted, while existing permission and account-deactivation behavior remains intact.

## Additional information

### Runtime evidence

- Before the workaround, a 20-second observation recorded repeated transcript disappearance, including ten content-state transitions.
- A bounded DOM diagnostic confirmed repeated replacement of the `contenteditable` element.
- React Fiber inspection identified `MJn` as the highest recreated component; its parent `vfi` retained its instance. The account-root key and the local-thread layout wrapper branch remained stable.

### Candidate root cause

In `webview/assets/app-initial-9cbfb5c07b41.js`, `vfi` receives an account-query error as `c` and alternates between a wrapper and its bare children:

```js
H = c == null ? jsx(S4e, { children: V }) : V;
```

`S4e` resolves to `MJn` (`nZ`) from `app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js`. This component always returns its children; it only reads the router location and uses memoization. Adding/removing it changes the React tree shape and recreates the descendant conversation and composer.

### Targeted local workaround

Keep that component mounted:

```js
H = jsx(S4e, { children: V });
```

The existing `m` permission/account-deactivation checks and `dfi` branch remain unchanged. No authentication, proxy, or backend configuration was changed by this workaround.

### Validation and limitations

The patched JavaScript passes syntax checking. An independent source review confirmed that the wrapper has no access-control behavior. After loading the patch, 65 read-only accessibility snapshots over 16 seconds showed persistent conversation content and composer, with no empty samples. Before the patch, the same symptom recurred within this observation duration.

This is a short observation, not a guarantee about all scenarios. Sustained use and real IME composition still need user verification. Temporary instrumentation was removed. Updating or reinstalling the extension may replace the local workaround.

### Suggested regression coverage

Render the authenticated local conversation while the account-query error transitions between absent and present/retrying. Verify that the conversation subtree and the composer DOM node retain identity and that IME composition is not interrupted. Preserve the existing account-deactivation and permission behavior.

items.title: Respect approval policies in temporary structured threads
items.body:
Respect approval policies in temporary structured threads

## Why

Forcing `approval_policy` to `never` on temporary structured threads can trigger configuration warnings when managed requirements allow only `on-request`. These hidden threads also need to reject unexpected interaction requests without prompting the user.

## What changed

Inherit the app server's approval policy when starting temporary structured threads. Reject their server requests before dynamic tool handling or interactive TUI routing.

## Testing

Extend regression tests to verify inherited `on-request` approval without approval-policy warnings, and error responses for recap-thread approval and user-input requests even when the thread is marked active and primary.
